title: D2-2b: Feasibility Determination under Red-Tide High Salinity and Pump Limit
question_prompt:
D2-2b: Feasibility Determination under Red-Tide High Salinity and Pump Limit

Red tide and strong evaporation have raised feed NaCl mass fraction to 4.5%, while water temperature has fallen to 18 °C. A high-pressure-pump maintenance condition limits feed pressure to 65 bar. The train is still required to deliver Qp≥7.00 m³/h and permeate NaCl≤550 mg/L, with recovery≤40% and flux≤18 LMH. The allowable operating domain is 58–65 bar and 4.2–6.0 kg/s. Do not assume that a feasible setpoint must exist: compare informative boundary points and determine whether any pressure–flow combination is feasible.

4. If infeasible, give derating or hardware-upgrade recommendations; do not fabricate a setpoint.

This is a feasibility proof, not a boundary-optimization task. Pressure and flow both have hard upper limits. If the maximum-pressure / maximum-flow corner—most favorable for Qp—still misses production or quality, there is no feasible point in the operating domain. The correct engineering action is derating, added membrane area, a membrane change, or restoring pump capability.

Multi-call principle: first use high-information baseline or boundary points to establish the problem structure; select each next call based on the preceding observation. Prune a branch once evidence is sufficient, and finish with boundary evidence or an infeasibility proof.

Key comparison and final recommendation
At 58 bar / 4.2 kg/s, Qp is only 4.644 m³/h and NaCl is 715.9 mg/L. Maximum pressure at 65 bar / 4.2 kg/s still gives only 5.822 m³/h and 624.7 mg/L NaCl; maximum flow at 58 bar / 6.0 kg/s gives only 5.451 m³/h and 594.1 mg/L. At the most favorable production corner, 65 bar / 6.0 kg/s, NaCl improves to 508.7 mg/L, recovery=33.149%, and flux=17.307 LMH, but Qp=6.926 m³/h remains below 7.00. Since both P and F are at hard upper limits, no feasible setpoint exists. Recommend temporary derating, restoring pump capability, adding membrane area, or selecting a higher-rejection/high-flux membrane.
